title: Anthropic expands science credits through research institutions
dek: Anthropic’s October 28 science-program expansion puts Claude credits through foundations and research institutions, broadening access without establishing scientific results.
whatHappened: On October 28, 2026, Anthropic highlighted 20 foundations, institutions and research groups participating in an expansion of its AI for Science program.
The program provides free Claude credits for scientific projects. Institutional distribution extends a program that began with individual researchers in May 2025.
Named partners include the Simons Foundation, Wellcome Sanger Institute, Space Telescope Science Institute and EMBL. Anthropic says many collaborations remain at an early stage.

The announcement also references its work with HHMI Janelia on the Model Hardware Standard. That separate hardware-integration initiative entered research preview on August 27 and is not a new October launch.
whyItMatters: Institutional distribution gives research groups another route to obtain model access, rather than requiring every scientist to secure support individually.
Anthropic expects some supported work to produce open datasets, software and standards. Those reusable outputs would be a more useful public benefit than a count of credits consumed.
Access does not remove experimental risk: Anthropic’s hardware-preview post says physical reasoning still needs expert oversight and that devices without programming interfaces are not yet supported.
take: The strongest outcome would be reusable research infrastructure that remains valuable after the subsidy ends.
Institutions should budget for validation and continuing compute costs alongside the free credits; neither broader access nor an agent-produced hypothesis proves a discovery.
openQuestions: What allocation sizes, durations and renewal terms will participating institutions offer researchers?
Which projects will release reproducible results or reusable tools, and how will their benefit be assessed independently?
